[[b]]Trial by Combat[[/b]]|| Challenge a Greatest Warrior serving in your faction and settle the matter in person. \\n\\n Warriors are fought. Scholars are debated.

Greatest Warriors serving in your faction can be challenged in person. The list refreshes at the start of each turn and every time you open this panel. Winning claims their trophy exactly as killing them in battle would, and counts toward the set. Losing locks that man for 3 turns before he will face you again.

ATTACK swings for full damage and can land a critical. GUARD cuts the incoming blow to 45 percent, restores 4 percent of your health and builds 2 Momentum, but cannot be used twice in a row. SPECIAL strikes for 2.2 times damage and ignores half his Defence, spending 3 Momentum. Whoever reaches zero first loses: a man who is put down does not swing back, so no exchange ends with both of you on the floor. Evenly matched men fall in about 8 rounds; if 12 rounds pass, whoever holds the greater share of his health wins on points.

Scholars are argued with rather than fought. Each round offers three topics drawn from what men of the age actually held opinions on. Argue a point he is on record OPPOSING and it lands hard. Argue one he HOLDS and he rebuts you with his own words. An untested point is a probe: it costs you a little, and reveals where he stands for the rest of the debate.

Lu Bu is a poor listener, and has options no heir inherits. PRETEND TO IGNORE may negate his entire point. INVOKE MY HALBERD settles a round on martial strength instead of wit, twice per debate. CHANGE THE SUBJECT discards all three topics. STARE BLANKLY costs him composure as he explains himself to a man who is not listening. FEIGN AGREEMENT buys you time and steadies you both. And once you have lost more than 65 percent of your composure, PUNCH THE NERD ends the argument permanently.

What a man carries changes who he is. Every equipped weapon, armour, mount, accessory and follower feeds his five attributes, and both contests derive their numbers from those. A blade that sharpens Instinct wins duels; a scholar's gift that deepens Cunning wins debates. Lu Bu also strikes harder for every trophy already in the cabinet.
Open the rules for the trial: how targets appear, how a duel and a debate are fought, Lu Bu's own methods, and how your equipment feeds into all of it.
